## Summary

I updated `HddsClientUtils.verifyResourceName(String, String, boolean)` in `/workspace/repo/hadoop-hdds/client/src/main/java/org/apache/hadoop/hdds/scm/client/HddsClientUtils.java` so that length validation is prioritized over content-based checks:

- Added a null guard (so the length check can safely call `resName.length()`).
- Added a minimum-length check at the very top of the method — before the character-scan loop and the all-numeric/IPv4 check. If the name is shorter than `OzoneConsts.OZONE_MIN_BUCKET_NAME_LENGTH` (3), it throws `IllegalArgumentException` with a message containing the phrase **`length is illegal`** (plus the resource type and the valid length range).

Because this runs first, a name that is both too short *and* all-numeric (e.g. `"12"`) now reports the length problem rather than the "cannot be an IPv4 address or all numeric" content error. The message intentionally does not embed the raw name, avoiding echoing potentially-malicious input for invalid short names.

I did not touch anything under `tests/`.
